report: CEE live-run COMPATIBILITY STOP (authorisation clauses 5 and 10)
status: STOPPED before any CEE paid cell; zero of the 44 authorised CEE calls executed; awaiting decision
summary: The provider-neutral STRICT json_schema required by the CEE design and by authorisation clause 5 is accepted by OpenAI gpt-4.1-mini but REJECTED (HTTP 400, 'This response_format type is unavailable now') by every current DeepSeek model tested. The refusal is at the response_format TYPE level (a 1-property minimal schema is rejected too), not caused by the CEE schema content. Per clause 5 a downgrade to json_object/plain_text is forbidden without approval, so the run was halted rather than silently changed.

diagnostic_call_cost_note: All probes used max_tokens=16 and trivial prompts; 400-rejected requests bill zero completion; successful probes were 2 (flash plain) + 1 (gpt strict 16 tok) + 2 (v4 json_object 16 tok) tokens, a few tenths of a US cent total and NOT counted among the 44 authorised CEE cells. No CEE bundle was ever sent to a model.

deepseek_lineup_change.finding: Official DeepSeek docs (api-docs.deepseek.com/quick_start/pricing, accessed 2026-10-23): current models are deepseek-v4-flash and deepseek-v4-pro; legacy aliases deepseek-chat/deepseek-reasoner were deprecated 2026-07-24. The E1 Wave-2.1 DeepSeek arm served model id 'deepseek-flash' (110 rows). The live endpoint now maps requests to the current backend (a json_object probe to deepseek-v4-flash returned served='deepseek-flash').
deepseek_lineup_change.feature_matrix: DeepSeek current docs list 'Json Output' as supported but no structured-output json_schema mode; empirical result: only json_object and plain are accepted.

why_this_is_not_a_schema_bug_we_can_fix: cee_review_decision_v1 is strict-legal (all 5 properties required, additionalProperties false, strict=true); it is exactly the shape OpenAI accepts. DeepSeek rejects the response_format TYPE itself for every schema, so no edit to our schema can make strict mode work on DeepSeek today.

options_for_decision.name: Keep identical STRICT schema on both (original clause 5 / P1 control)
options_for_decision.feasibility: NOT EXECUTABLE against DeepSeek today (endpoint lacks the capability). Would require waiting for DeepSeek to ship json_schema, or routing DeepSeek through a gateway that emulates strict mode (new dependency, changes the serving stack - not pre-approved).
options_for_decision.scientific_cost: none if it were available; currently blocks CEE indefinitely

options_for_decision.name: Both providers on json_object (the ONLY common denominator DeepSeek accepts)
options_for_decision.description: Send {type:json_object} to BOTH models, keep the identical cee_review_decision_v1 JSON CONTRACT, system/user prompt, bundles and the explicit 5-key instruction sentence; the parser already scores INVALID/AMBIGUOUS for any non-conforming output. This preserves 'identical task, identical JSON contract, identical request shape type' while sacrificing server-side schema enforcement on both sides.
options_for_decision.tradeoff: Re-introduces the exact E1 format difference in reverse: in E1 DS=strict/GPT=json_object; under B both are json_object, so the format mode is at least IDENTICAL across the two CEE arms (a cleaner control than E1), but neither arm gets wire-level schema enforcement. Any malformed JSON is counted, never auto-corrected.
options_for_decision.change_required: authorise json_object for CEE (a CEE-specific wire-mode amendment); freeze a new CEE protocol/prompt fingerprint version; re-run offline selftest; then execute 44 calls.

options_for_decision.name: Asymmetric but documented (GPT strict, DeepSeek json_object)
options_for_decision.description: Run GPT with strict and DeepSeek with json_object, recording the difference as a known API constraint (mirrors what each vendor can do).
options_for_decision.tradeoff: VIOLATES clause 4/5 identical-constraint requirement and preserves the format confound the study was designed to remove; NOT recommended; listed for completeness.

options_for_decision.name: Run GPT arm only now (22 calls), defer DeepSeek arm
options_for_decision.description: Execute the 22 gpt-4.1-mini CEE calls that are fully unblocked; hold DeepSeek until json_schema ships or option B is approved.
options_for_decision.tradeoff: Partial result; cannot compute the paired cross-model contrast which is the entire point of CEE; reported as a one-arm descriptive run only.

options_for_decision.name: Hold CEE; no paid run
options_for_decision.description: Leave the frozen offline design as-is and revisit when DeepSeek supports json_schema; pursue other approved work in the meantime.
options_for_decision.tradeoff: no new spend; mechanism-isolation question stays open

recommendation: B, if the scientific priority is executing the mechanism-isolation experiment now: json_object on BOTH arms keeps the request-shape TYPE identical across providers (the controllable part) and keeps the JSON contract/prompt/bundles byte-identical; wire-level schema strictness is unavailable on DeepSeek regardless, so forcing strict cannot add control there. The design freeze, fingerprint and selftest would be version-bumped under a new CEE revision; existing cee-fixed-v1 artifacts stay untouched. Options A/D/E remain valid if strict wire enforcement is considered indispensable.
